chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash'ari narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ismā'īl al-Ju'fi, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray Dhuhr when the shadow of the wall was one cubit, and when it was two cubits, he would pray 'Asr.
I said, 'Indeed, the wall varies; some parts are short and some are long.'
He said, 'The wall of the Prophet's mosque (peace be upon him and his family) at that time was one qamah (standing height).
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad determine the specific times for Dhuhr and Asr prayers using shadows?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of shadow measurement (qibla-based timekeeping) for determining prayer times, a method widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. The clarification regarding the 'qamah' (approximately 4-5 cubits) of the Prophet’s mosque wall anchors the abstract cubit measurements to a tangible historical standard, ensuring consistency in ritual timing. This reflects the Shia emphasis on deriving legal rulings from specific historical contexts while maintaining universal applicability through standardized references.
